5.3a — Into the Cave: Scene Loading & Mode Switch

You break the door, you walk in — and the game you are playing quietly becomes a different game. Today: how ONE player script runs as a top-down character on the surface and a platformer underground, decided by nothing but the scene's own name.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the branch in PlayerController.Start:

private bool isPlatformer;

private void Start()
{
    string sceneName = SceneManager.GetActiveScene().name;
    if (sceneName == "Platformer" || sceneName == "Start")
    {
        isPlatformer = true;
        rb.gravityScale = 0;
    }
}

Wait — read it again, slowly. "Platformer" and "Start" set isPlatformer = true... and then set gravity to 0? That reads backwards — until you learn the starter's naming: the "Start" scene IS the top-down overworld (that is where you respawned in 2.2a), and "Platformer" is the cave scene. Top-down means NO gravity — a top-down character who falls is a broken top-down character. The bool's name is the confession: isPlatformer means "we are in a scene where the movement style is top-down-or-platformer, not pure physics." Trace which scene you are IN before you judge any branch.

Predict: the player walks into the cave door area. What must happen to the WHOLE world to put you in a platformer — same scene with a camera pan, or a brand-new scene load? Where did you last see SceneManager.LoadScene, and who called it?

Socratic

One component behaving differently per scene is the instance idea: every scene gets its own Player object, each with the same script but different rules. What is saved between scenes (StatManager!) and what is born fresh — and why do coins survive the door but position cannot?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — open the cave. The starter ships a Platformer scene (Assets/Scenes — check it exists; if your fork names it differently, use YOUR name and update the string in Start). Wire the cave door's lever event (5.2a) or a new trigger to:

SceneManager.LoadScene("Platformer");

Run it. The whole world is swapped in one frame. The Console from the overworld is gone, the enemies are gone, the coins are gone — everything except what a DontDestroyOnLoad singleton carries. Walk around: the same PlayerController

Step 2 — feel the mode. In the cave scene, try WASD: vertical input does something DIFFERENT now — or nothing, depending on how the branch is built. Read Update's isPlatformer branch: which input does the platformer branch ignore, and what does top-down use instead of AddForce for movement? Your movement table from 1.4a gets a second column today.

Step 3 — the physics flip. Top-down: gravityScale 0, vertical ySpeed translation. Platformer physics: gravity ON, and jump via AddForce Impulse. Same script, opposite physics. Change gravityScale in the Inspector while in the cave — watch your character fall like a stone (2) or float like a moon astronaut (0.05). THAT is the number you will tune in 6.1a.

Bug Hunt: The wrong-world player

  1. Rename the Platformer scene to "Cave" in the Project window but do NOT update the string in Start. Describe every symptom, then find it — how long did the silent-string hunt take this time?
  2. Load the Platformer scene directly (File → Play from that scene) without breaking the door. Does the game work — and why is that both a feature and a bug?
  3. In the cave, the E-key lever scan runs. Place a lever in the cave and press E. Is the interaction system overworld-only — should it be?
  4. The overworld keeps gravityScale 0 in Start. Delete that line and press Play in the overworld. Where did the player go — and why did "falls forever" look like "nothing happened"?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Mode design

  1. Coins carry across the door (singleton) but your position does not. Design the respawn contract: if you die in the cave, where do you wake — and what does LoadScene("Start") from 2.2a already give you?
  2. Add a second cave scene ("Cave2") and a door deeper in. What strings must match now — and would a scene-name LIST be better than an if?
  3. Commit + push: "5.3a: door opens, mode switches, physics flips".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain the scene-name branch and the (confusing) isPlatformer/gravityScale pairing
  • Load a scene from code and from an event
  • Explain what survives a scene change (singletons) and what does not
  • Tune gravityScale and describe what it changes about the genre
